chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from 'Isa ibn Sabih said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the thief who steals from the top (of a garment), the thief who steals from the bottom, and the pickpocket. He said: 'They are not amputated.' The way to reconcile these two reports is to apply the distinction contained in the first two reports: that if the thief from the top takes from the upper part of the shirt, there is no amputation upon him; and if he takes from the lower part, amputation is obligatory upon him.

key_terms.الطَّرَّار: Thief who steals from the top/upper part
key_terms.النَّبَّاش: Thief who steals from the bottom/lower part

ai.seo_question: When is hand amputation obligatory for a thief stealing from clothing according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) resolves the apparent contradiction in previous reports regarding the thief's amputation by distinguishing between the upper and lower parts of a garment, establishing that the ruling applies only when the lower portion is taken. This specific jurisprudential nuance highlights the Shia method of reconciling hadiths through contextual differentiation rather than abrogation. It underscores the precision required in applying hudud penalties, ensuring they are not applied broadly but only under strictly defined conditions of theft.
